deep.reconstruction:
Setting: steady flow of water through a curved tube MN of variable cross-section zz, fed from the top AB (x vertical downward, s arc length, Φ the angle of the tube with the vertical). The flux is fixed, so the speed is u = b²√v/z². Euler's units are g = 1/2 with forces written as 2·d²x/dt², which makes gravity = 1 and pressures heights p.

1. From the previous page the tangential acceleration is 2u du/ds = −4b⁴v dz/(z⁵ ds). This is just the convective acceleration of a quasi-one-dimensional flow.
2. Three tangential forces act on an element:
   - gravity, cos Φ;
   - the pressure gradient, −dp/ds;
   - friction, taken (§11) as a retarding force αp/z. It is proportional to the local pressure ('status compressionis') and inversely to the linear size z of the section, as in Coulomb/Amontons friction proportional to normal load.
3. Newton along the tube: −4b⁴v dz/(z⁵ds) = cos Φ − dp/ds − αp/z. With ds cos Φ = dx this becomes the linear first-order ODE dp + αp ds/z = dx + 4b⁴v dz/z⁵. This is a one-dimensional Bernoulli/momentum equation with a loss term.
4. Integrating factor: with r = ∫ds/z, multiplying by e^{αr} gives e^{αr}p = C + ∫e^{αr}dx + 4b⁴v∫e^{αr}dz/z⁵.
5. Normalize r = 0 at the top (x = 0). Since α is very small, expand e^{αr} in its power series. This gives p as a perturbation series in α: the frictionless Bernoulli solution C + x − b⁴v/z⁴, plus corrections in α, α², ….
6. §24, continued on the next page: integration by parts using dr = ds/z gives the closed form p = Ce^{−αr} + x − αe^{−αr}∫e^{αr}x ds/z − b⁴v/z⁴ + αb⁴v e^{−αr}∫e^{αr}ds/z⁵. The constant C is fixed later by boundary conditions; §25ff treat a vessel plus an inclined pipe.
errors: In the series of §23 the friction-correction terms coming from 4b⁴v∫e^{αr}dz/z⁵ are printed with minus signs: −4αb⁴v∫r dz/z⁵ − 2α²b⁴v∫rr dz/z⁵ − (2/3)α³b⁴v∫r³dz/z⁵. Expanding 4b⁴v∫(1 + αr + α²r²/2 + …)dz/z⁵ gives + signs for all of them; only the leading term −b⁴v/z⁴ is negative. Euler's own closed form on the next page (+αb⁴v e^{−αr}∫e^{αr}ds/z⁵) is consistent with the + signs, so these are slips of sign (typesetting or computation).

Physically, the friction law (resistance ∝ pressure p / z rather than ∝ u²/D as in Chézy/Darcy–Weisbach) is not correct for fluids. It is a hypothesis carried over from solid (Coulomb/Amontons) friction, not a mathematical error.

ideas.what: Quasi-one-dimensional steady momentum balance along a curved tube of variable section, including convective acceleration, gravity, pressure gradient and a wall-friction term
ideas.modern_name: Generalized (lossy) Bernoulli equation / one-dimensional pipe-flow momentum equation
ideas.usually_credited_to: Daniel Bernoulli (Hydrodynamica 1738) for the lossless case; head-loss forms to Chézy (1770s), Weisbach (1845) and Darcy (1857)
ideas.where_published: E260 itself (Novi Comm. Petrop. 6, 1756/57, publ. 1761); related pipe-flow work in Euler's hydraulic papers of the 1750s

ideas.what: Friction resistance proportional to the internal pressure and inversely to tube size (αp/z)
ideas.modern_name: Coulomb-type (pressure-dependent) wall friction hypothesis for fluids
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (E260), discussed in histories of hydraulics

ideas.what: Integrating factor e^{α∫ds/z} for the linear ODE in p
ideas.modern_name: Integrating factor for a first-order linear ODE
ideas.where_published: Many Euler works, e.g. Institutiones calculi integralis

ideas.what: Expansion of the solution in powers of the small friction coefficient α, plus integration by parts to obtain a closed form
ideas.modern_name: Regular perturbation expansion in a small parameter

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine derivation within Euler's known (and physically superseded) pressure-proportional friction model for pipe flow. The integration techniques are standard. The paper and its friction hypothesis are already noted in histories of hydraulics, so nothing appears overlooked beyond a minor sign slip.
transcription_corrections: The transcription faithfully reproduces the printed minus signs in the α-series of §23 ('−4αb⁴v∫rdz/z⁵ − 2α²b⁴v∫rrdz/z⁵ − (2/3)α³b⁴v∫r³dz/z⁵ − etc.'). These match the image but are mathematically wrong (they should be +).
The catchword at the foot of the page is '∫e^{αr}' (the scan looks like 'e^{qr}').
